_doc: A/B test plan for @itsongit. pipeline/plan.py assigns arms per day, pipeline/experiments.py reports. Reels before 'started' are the baseline (all hook=price). Format test (classic vs story) since 2026-11-02.

windows.why: 11-12h Berlin: 10 reels, median 100+ views (best median of any hour band)
18-19h: 9 reels, mean 119 (best mean); studies agree early evening is strong for Reels
20-23h median only ~25, but the Mixxx breakout (22:48) landed here and studies favour 8 PM-midnight: kept as the measured third window

dropped_windows.13:00-14:59: 16 reels, median 33-44 views: the dead zone (moved later, to the evening)
dropped_windows.07:00-09:00: never tested; candidate for the next window test if night stays weak

format.question: Does the animated story format (Kit the cat, beats, whip pans) beat the classic ad template?

arms.classic: the price-card / demo-hook template (then split A/B by the hook test)
arms.story: animated explainer: hook slam on frame 0, Kit reacting with lip sync, versus/app/list/counter scenes, whip pans, re-hooks, 22-35 s

format.decide: story wins if its median views beat classic by 30%+ with no worse skip rate: then it becomes 2 of 3 daily reels (and 3 of 3 if it wins again over the next 12). Classic wins if story isn't ahead after 12 each.

hook.question: Does showing the app in action on frame 0 cut the 3-second skip rate?

arms.price: A: HyperFrames price-slash text card (control, every reel so far)
arms.demo: B: app-in-action cold open, job line on top, struck price strip below (same voiceover)

hook.decide: B wins if its median skip rate is at least 5 points lower than A's AND its median views are not lower. A wins if B is not better after 15 per arm. Then make the winner the default and test the next hook idea against it.
hook.note: From 2026-11-02 only classic-format reels run the hook test (half the classic rows each).

topic.question: Which kind of 'everyone pays for this' pick travels furthest?

arms.subscription: replaces a famous monthly/yearly subscription (Adobe, Canva, Grammarly, Office…)
arms.utility: desktop/phone utility that fixes a daily annoyance (Magnet, Paste, CleanMyMac…)
arms.hobby: creative/hobby tool where the paid app is famous in that hobby (Serato, Photoshop…)

topic.decide: After 10 per arm, give the best arm 2 of the 3 daily reels; keep 1 rotating so the others keep being measured.
topic.banned: developer, academic and pro-only tools (the 'niche' baseline group: median views far below the rest)

dev_line.status: ready (labs/dev-line has the first 5 builds; not posted yet)
dev_line.question: Does a developer-first line (terminal tools, self-hosting, AI coding repos) earn more views/follows per reel than the consumer 'free alternative' line?

arms.consumer: current story/classic reels: famous paid consumer app -> free repo
arms.dev: developer-first story reels: video.json "line": "dev" (listicle, replace-paid-dev-tool, one-command, before/after)

dev_line.decide: dev wins if its median views are within 20% of consumer AND shares+saves/100 or follows/100 are higher (devs save and share tools): then 1 of 3 daily slots becomes dev. Dev loses if median views < 60% of consumer after 10.
dev_line.note: Baseline warning: earlier dev picks (opencode, hoppscotch) posted as consumer-style reels landed in the 'niche' group. This test changes the framing (dev hooks, dev visuals), not just the topic.

visual_theme.status: ready (labs/dev-line/t1-shell-{crt,keynote,paper}: same script + same voice, 3 skins)
visual_theme.question: Inside the dev line, which skin holds attention best: Lemo-Opuscar 'crt' terminal, 'keynote' dark launch, 'blueprint' drawing, or our 'paper' + Kit?

arms.clay: clay stop-motion dialogue: Kit asks, an assistant character answers (two voices)

visual_theme.decide: A skin wins if its median skip rate is 5+ points below paper's and its median watch time is not lower. Rotate skins across dev reels, never two of the same skin on one day.
visual_theme.how: video.json "theme": paper|crt|keynote|blueprint (studio/src/themes.tsx). Kit is on for paper, off for the others unless "mascot": true.

dev_hook.status: ready (labs/dev-line/t2-coolify-{money,result}: same body, different first 2 beats)
dev_hook.question: For developer reels, does a money-leak hook beat a result-first 'one command' hook?

arms.money-leak: "You're paying Vercel twenty dollars a month..." (price slam on frame 0)
arms.result-first: "This one command turns any server into your own Vercel" (live typed terminal on frame 0)

dev_hook.decide: result-first wins with 5+ points lower median skip; then live-terminal openers become the dev default.
dev_hook.how: video.json "hook_type" is stamped into post.json experiment.hook

windows_note: Analysed by real Berlin posting time. The old slot numbers only picked the accent colour (times were already randomised).

ideas_next.name: withheld-payoff hook (consumer line)
ideas_next.idea: Hooks currently reveal 'price -> $0' in the first second, closing the loop. Test a hook that names the pain and the result but withholds the app until ~5-7 s ('I cancelled a $144/yr subscription last week. What replaced it costs nothing.'), against the current money-leak opener. Primary: avg watch time.
ideas_next.why: avg watch is 5-7 s of 25-40 s; the skills put the first retention cliff right after the loop closes

ideas_next.name: live-typed hook text on frame 0 (consumer line)
ideas_next.from: virality skill: same line 522 views as a static card vs 35,834 typed live in the real app
ideas_next.idea: Type the hook line into a search bar / app UI on frame 0 instead of slamming it as a static word block.
